utterance: Hi Chloe, thanks for coming in today. Can you tell me more about the burning when you go to the toilet?
reply: It really stings and burns, especially right at the end of weeing. I'm going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out so I always have to rush. This started yesterday morning, so it has been about a day and a half. It looks a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had anything like this before?
reply: I had one similar thing happen about two years ago, but that is it.

utterance: Do you have any pain anywhere, like in your lower belly or back?
reply: Just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy above my bladder, and nothing in my back.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Abdominal pain beyond a low ache
Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)

utterance: How many sexual partners have you had in the last month?
reply: Um, yeah, I have a boyfriend and we have been together about a year. He is my only partner.

utterance: Have you noticed any unusual discharge or anything else unusual?
reply: I haven't noticed anything like that.

utterance: Do you feel generally unwell or have a fever?
reply: I am eating normally and haven't been sick, and I don't have any fevers or shivers. I feel fine apart from this.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell
Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking

finding: Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.

utterance: Do you use protection when having sex, like condoms?
reply: I am on the pill and I do not miss it, so we do not use condoms.

utterance: I'm going to get some urine sent off to the lab to check for infection. In the meantime, I'll give you some antibiotics to start treating the infection. We'll review the results when they come back.
reply: Oh, great, can I just get the script now so I can drop it off at the pharmacy and get back to work?

utterance: You should start feeling better within a few days. If your symptoms don't improve or get worse, come back and see me. Also, if you develop any new symptoms like back pain or fever, come back straight away.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days
Defensible diagnosis: Lower urinary tract infection
